name: Comedy Engine v3 (기본)
description: 기본 제공 프리셋입니다. 코미디 원문(Comedy Engine v3)을 이 화면에서 직접 고쳐 저장하세요. 저장해도 이 기본값은 언제든 '기본값 복원'으로 되돌릴 수 있습니다.

sections.generationInstructions:
Write the script from the approved concept without changing its premise. The episode follows the FIXED SERIES FORMULA (the application enforces its structure):
PART A — a unique, escalating, absurd comedy story with SIX mandatory beats in order: 도입(setup), 위기 1(problem), 위기 2(absurd escalation), 절정(unexpected twist), 결말(resolution), 제품 연결(product bridge). A beat may use several scenes.
PART B — the fixed three-shot product ending is added by the application from the selected ending template. Do NOT write it.
- Preserve every story beat the operator already wrote (USER_STORY_BEATS) as the premise of that beat.
- The first 3 seconds contain the hook. Each beat has one clear comedic purpose; the escalation must be the SAME problem pushed to a cartoonish extreme.
- The twist must be directly connected to the escalating problem (background-world absurdity, unexpected character behaviour); never unrelated randomness.
- Connect the story to the product only through CONSEQUENCES in the product bridge, never through forced advertising. The product does not appear in Part A.
- Jack's confidence, stubbornness and dry humour against Diane's energy: keep their personalities consistent.
sections.comedyLevel1: COMEDY INTENSITY 1 (gentle): warm, relatable, low-key humour. Mostly observational and dialogue-driven. Small, believable reactions; no slapstick; no exaggerated shouting.
sections.comedyLevel2: COMEDY INTENSITY 2 (balanced, default): clear comedic beats in most scenes. Mix of dry one-liners and expressive reactions. One or two exaggerated visual gags per reel. Keep the situation believable.
sections.comedyLevel3: COMEDY INTENSITY 3 (high energy): big escalation, exaggerated reactions, fast cuts and visual absurdity (still anchored in a real household problem). Strong running gag and callback. Diane's excitement and Jack's stubbornness are pushed to the extreme, but the product facts stay accurate.
sections.characterRules:
CHARACTERS
- Diane: Korean wife, long black hair, energetic, impulsive shopper. When she is excited she may shout "BABYYYY!!!!!!" (do not force it into every scene). Diane NEVER calls Jack "오빠".
- Jack: British husband, muscular/stocky, brown wavy hair, thick mustache, tattooed arms, affectionate dry humour; understated and a little stubborn.
- Spoken dialogue is in English. Keep each line short enough to be spoken in the scene's duration.
- Character reference sheets are identity guides only; one Jack means exactly one Jack, one Diane exactly one Diane.
sections.subtitleStyle:
KOREAN SUBTITLES
- Each dialogue line has a separate Korean subtitle (ko). It must not be a copy of the English line.
- Natural, spoken Korean (casual, as a Korean viewer would say it); keep the joke's timing. Short: ideally one line, at most two short lines.
- Do not translate word for word; adapt the joke. Keep "BABYYYY" as is.
sections.sceneStructure:
SCENE STRUCTURE (fixed formula)
- Part A: exactly the six beats in this order: setup, problem, absurd_escalation, unexpected_twist, resolution, product_bridge. Each beat has a Korean beat title, an English story description, visual direction and one or more scenes (3-6 seconds each).
- Every scene has a short meaningful Korean title (title_ko) naming its key action or comedic beat.
- Part B (three product-ending shots) is appended by the application; never create a fourth ending shot. The affiliate disclosure / CTA is an overlay or end card, not a story shot.
sections.productIntegration:
PRODUCT INTEGRATION
- The story reaches the product only in the product bridge, as a believable household consequence that gives Diane a natural excuse to buy.
- Product facts come only from the verified facts provided. Never invent specifications, prices, discounts, availability or performance claims. Do not change the product's shape, logo or colour.
- For the product-specific ending variables, use the real product name and only verified, visible functionality.
